why: The answer compares the do-while with a while loop and correctly says which starting values make them behave differently: they match when i starts at 70 or above and differ only when i starts below 70. That reasoning goes beyond the given code, although it never actually gives the output for 61 (which would be "61 " from the one pass the do-while always makes).

concepts.quote: With a while loop the output is the same here, because 81 >= 70 is true at the start; it would only differ if i started below 70.
concepts.why: It correctly says that a while loop whose condition is false at the start runs zero times, so it differs from the do-while exactly when i starts below 70.
It correctly evaluates the loop condition with the starting value of i, but it only uses the condition in this one place.
